headline: Ecuador stuns Germany 2-1 to reach World Cup knockout stage
summary: A dramatic comeback victory in their final Group E match secures a place in the last 32 for the South American side.
details: Ecuador defeated Germany 2-1 in their final Group E match on Thursday, securing a place in the knockout stage of the World Cup. Needing a win to keep their hopes alive, Ecuador overcame an early deficit to advance to the last 32.

Germany took an early lead in the second minute when Leroy Sane scored, but Ecuador responded in the ninth minute with a curled strike from Nilson Angulo. The match remained tied until the 78th minute when Gonzalo Plata scored the winning goal.

The victory marks a historic achievement for Ecuador, who had struggled in their first two matches of the tournament. The team's determination and faith paid off as they qualified as one of the best eight third-placed teams.

Germany, despite the loss, finished top of Group E with six points. However, the result exposed defensive vulnerabilities, with the German side conceding goals in all three of their group stage matches.

The match took place at a sold-out stadium in New York/New Jersey, where a massive crowd of Ecuadorian fans celebrated the historic win. Players expressed their gratitude to the fans for making them feel at home throughout the tournament.

headline: Pepe double seals Ivory Coast's first World Cup knockout trip
summary: Nicolas Pepe scored twice to secure a 2-0 win over Curacao, sending Ivory Coast to the knockout phase for the first time in their history.
details: Nicolas Pepe's double sealed Ivory Coast's first trip to the World Cup knockout phase with a 2-0 victory over Curacao on Thursday.
The win ensures Ivory Coast finishes second in Group E, marking a historic milestone for the team after failing to reach the knockouts in their previous three appearances from 2006-2014.
Pepe, who had not scored in five World Cup qualifying matches and was left out of the recent AFCON squad, became the hero of the match.
The first goal came from a low first-time finish after 19-year-old Yan Diomande pounced on a Curacao error and provided the assist.
Pepe's second goal was a curled finish from 10 metres inside the left post, following a perfect through ball from Ibrahim Sangare.
Curacao, the smallest nation to ever qualify for the World Cup finals, became the eighth team eliminated from the tournament.
Ivory Coast will now face the second-place team from Group I, France or Norway, on Tuesday in Arlington, Texas.
Despite the loss, Curacao had moments of threat, with Leandro Bacuna and Sherel Floranus coming close to scoring.
Amad Diallo, the team's first goalscorer in the tournament, was substituted at halftime, though it was unclear if this was due to injury.
caption:
History made! 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast reaches the World Cup knockout phase for the first time ever.

Nicolas Pepe's double sealed Ivory Coast's first trip to the World Cup knockout phase with a 2-0 victory over Curacao on Thursday.

The win ensures Ivory Coast finishes second in Group E, marking a historic milestone for the team after failing to reach the knockouts in their previous three appearances from 2006-2014.

Pepe, who had not scored in five World Cup qualifying matches and was left out of the recent AFCON squad, became the hero of the match.

The first goal came from a low first-time finish after 19-year-old Yan Diomande pounced on a Curacao error and provided the assist.

Pepe's second goal was a curled finish from 10 metres inside the left post, following a perfect through ball from Ibrahim Sangare.

Curacao, the smallest nation to ever qualify for the World Cup finals, became the eighth team eliminated from the tournament.

Ivory Coast will now face the second-place team from Group I, France or Norway, on Tuesday in Arlington, Texas.

Despite the loss, Curacao had moments of threat, with Leandro Bacuna and Sherel Floranus coming close to scoring.

Amad Diallo, the team's first goalscorer in the tournament, was substituted at halftime, though it was unclear if this was due to injury.
